stream_log.reasoning: Week of 2026-10-19 to 10-26. Two threads defined the week: a record-tempo escalation of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz war and the first concrete US-Israel preparations to strike Iran since summer. On ~Oct 22 Iran's state media/IRGC claimed seven oil tankers were struck or mined in a single day - if confirmed, the largest single-day vessel toll since the war began in February - amid a record October attack tempo (28+ attacks in the month, 11+ VLCCs hit in October, 30+ damaged since February per a Reuters review of IMO/MarineTraffic data). Commercial transit collapsed to ~4 vessels/day vs a typical ~85 (IMF PortWatch, Oct 18), with 135 ships having turned around since the Jul 14 blockade began. This drives supply_chain_resilience 0.41->0.39 (the chokepoint stress decisively worsened again - record attack tempo, a seven-tanker day, traffic crashing to single digits) and middle_east_stability 0.10->0.09 (war escalated to a new threshold, plus continuing Houthi strikes on Saudi airports/Aramco facilities; kept to -0.01 because the dimension is already deep in crisis territory and the US stayed restrained, holding kinetic fire until after the Nov 3 midterms). The fresh oil shock lifted Brent to a new cycle high ~$114.72-116.72 on Oct 23 (highest since April/May, +~3-5% on the week, breaking above the ~$110 Oct 16 and ~$107 September peaks) before easing ~2% to ~$115 by Oct 26 on tentative de-escalation hopes/profit-taking; markets turned risk-off and stagflationary (S&P 500 ~7,623.68 Friday, ~-0.5% on the week with nearly 3 of 4 stocks falling and energy the only winner, Nasdaq ~25,955), so global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 0.99->0.98 as the renewed ~$115 oil shock transmits further - a small tick because equities fell far less than last week's -2%/-4% rout and oil came off its high by Friday. The week's sharpest strategic-escalation signal lifts nuclear_risk_level 0.37->0.39: the New York Times reported the US and Israel have drafted detailed plans for a brief (~3-day) intensive campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 midterms explicitly targeting NUCLEAR SITES, energy infrastructure and missile/drone capabilities, Trump and Netanyahu renewed strike threats (Trump weighing a deal vs. 'finish them off'), and Iran threatened a broader response including strikes on data centers and undersea communications cables - the most concrete pre-kinetic, nuclear-relevant buildup against a latent-nuclear adversary in weeks, scored +0.02 (more concrete than the +0.01 third-carrier buildup or the Poland/Estonia incursions), partially reversing recent easing. Sustained two-front high-intensity combat (the Hormuz/Gulf maritime war with seven tankers hit and seafarer casualties, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, daily Russia-Ukraine strikes killing civilians in Kyiv/Kharkiv, and Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan with reported civilian deaths) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,554,000->1,557,500 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: russia_stability stays 0.20 - the week was diplomacy-dominated (Zelensky-Witkoff-Stubb-Store talks in Oslo Oct 20, Kushner remote; Witkoff also met Putin in Moscow) with souring US-Ukraine ties (Trump again called for a new Ukraine leader; Kyiv accused Washington of leveraging aid/tech access to pressure it to halt refinery strikes, and the US reportedly asked for a strike pause), so despite the ongoing deep-strike campaign there was no fresh discrete internal shock to Russia this week, and the US pressure to pause refinery strikes slightly offsets - no decisive single-week mover. No new node: the Hormuz escalation (seven-tanker day, record tempo) is a severe development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, and the US-Israel strike plans are drafted contingency plans, not a consummated event - an actual major US/Israeli strike on Iranian nuclear sites, or a signed US-Iran or Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, would warrant a node - consistent with this log's node discipline. Watched but not scored: no confirmed frontier-AI flagship landed in-window (Gemini 4 still in post-training) after the early-September wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual cyber-damage surge; Venezuela opposition leader Maria Corina Machado's return from exile, Brazil's presidential vote, renewed France unrest, the UK North Sea gas approval, and Uganda's 21-day quarantine over the DRC Ebola outbreak were geopolitically/epidemiologically notable but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-10-26 to 11-02. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz war pushed chokepoint stress to a new extreme even as the very end of the window showed the first signs of a turn. Shipping through Hormuz slowed 'almost to a standstill' over the weekend, the UAE reported three ADNOC-operated vessels attacked in transit, more tankers were struck (two IRGC-claimed mine incidents on an 'unauthorised route', a projectile hit east of Saudi Arabia's Ras Al Khafji and a gas tanker in the strait), and Iran singled out South Korean operator Sinokor for enforcement from Nov 1, while Trump renewed military threats ('the hammer') and the US said it could hold the naval blockade indefinitely. Brent hit a fresh cycle high (~$113 Jan / ~$117 Dec contract on Oct 30, +13.6% on the month, a fourth straight weekly rally) before Qatar-mediated de-escalation hopes and an OPEC+ output path sent crude down ~4.3% to ~$100 on Nov 2. This drives supply_chain_resilience 0.39->0.38 (shipping to near-standstill, a Gulf state's own fleet directly hit, Brent at a new cycle high); kept to -0.01 because the late-week relief suggests peak stress may be passing, and middle_east_stability is held at 0.09 (the UAE/enforcement escalation and the emerging Qatar talks plus Trump's pre-midterm restraint roughly offset within an already-saturated crisis, and the chokepoint worsening is captured via supply_chain). global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 0.98->0.97 on a clearly risk-off, stagflationary week: the Nasdaq fell ~2% to close its worst month since March 2025 (~-5.3%) on disappointing Alphabet/Amazon/Intel earnings, the S&P 500 dropped to 7,580 in its worst session since June 5, all while oil sat at cycle highs for most of the week - a small tick, kept to -0.01 because the Nov-1/2 oil crash and midterm/de-escalation hopes relieve the drag at the window's close and could reverse it. Sustained two-front high-intensity combat (the Hormuz/Gulf maritime war, daily Russia-Ukraine strikes with renewed Ukrainian deep strikes on Russian refineries, Yemen/Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,557,500->1,561,000 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: nuclear_risk_level stays 0.39 - the drafted US-Israel plan for a post-midterm strike on Iranian nuclear sites still looms and Trump's threats continued, but no new kinetic strike landed, the stated trigger (the Nov 3 midterms) had not yet arrived, and late-week diplomacy offered a small offset, so no decisive single-week mover; russia_stability holds at 0.20 - the resumed refinery deep-strike campaign sustains economic pressure but is a continuation rather than a fresh discrete internal shock, and ISW assessed Russia's Fortress Belt encirclement plan as operationally stalled/defeated (Dobropillya/Serhiivka axes), so no clean stability mover; food_security_index holds at 0.71 absent a fresh grain/supply signal. No new node: every thread is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis and 2022_russia_ukraine wars - no signed US-Iran or Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, no actual major strike on Iranian nuclear sites, and no direct NATO-Russia war materialized (a mutual Russia/Ukraine air-raid-alert-app cyberattack sent false nuclear/chemical warnings on Nov 2 but is disinformation, not a real nuclear-weapons escalation). Watched but not scored: the US midterms (Tue Nov 3) are the week's biggest looming event but fall in the next window and are a scheduled election, not an era-defining discrete node; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra/Sol, Google's gated cyber-defender Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 28) after the early-September flagship wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual damage surge; and the Oct 22 Tibet M7.0 and Oct 9 Panama M7.7 earthquakes predate or edge this window and, like prior regional quakes/cyclones in this stream, map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.

Week of 2026-11-02 to 11-09. Two threads dominated: a US electoral realignment and the sharpest de-escalation turn of the 2026 Iran war to date. The feared post-midterm US-Israel strike on Iranian NUCLEAR sites - the drafted contingency that drove last week's nuclear-risk buildup - did NOT materialize. Instead the US ran only 'minor' conventional strikes (surface-to-air missiles near Hormuz on the Nov 3 midterm eve, air defenses on Qeshm Island Nov 6 that Trump explicitly called 'minor,' and a Nov 7 task force to interdict Iran's overland weapons shipments), while Qatar-mediated diplomacy accelerated: Iran pushed a plan to reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks, Trump signaled progress, and Trump was set to meet the Qatari PM on Nov 9 to discuss a ceasefire and nuclear talks. Markets priced the turn hard - Brent crude crashed ~13% on the week (its steepest weekly decline since March 2020) and ~18% from the Oct 30 high to the Nov 5 low, settling ~$98 Nov 6, on Middle East breakthrough hopes and analyst bets that a weakened administration will quit the war after the midterm 'shellacking,' with Kpler data indicating Hormuz flows recovering. This drives nuclear_risk_level 0.39->0.37 (the nuclear-site strike threat lapsed, only minor conventional strikes landed, Iran is offering to resume nuclear talks - reversing the Oct 26 +0.02 buildup tick), middle_east_stability 0.09->0.11 (real de-escalation turn and oil crash, kept to +0.02 because no ceasefire was signed, strikes and tanker attacks continued, and Iran's public position wobbled), and supply_chain_resilience 0.38->0.41 (the largest single move, warranted by the steepest weekly oil fall since 2020 and recovering Hormuz transit after many weeks of grinding chokepoint stress). On the US midterms (Nov 3), Democrats swept both chambers of Congress (projected 250+ House seats and a flipped Senate); Trump initially said he would accept the results before blaming Democrats and calling it 'one of the Worst Days in History.' This orderly, accepted election delivering a decisive legislative check on the executive nudges governance_model 0.48->0.49 (restoration of divided-government checks, a modest move toward liberal-democratic governance) and us_institutional_trust 0.25->0.26 (the electoral system worked and produced a peaceful opposition check); us_polarization holds at 0.72 as the decisive popular verdict and the peaceful transfer roughly offset Trump's acrimony, no clean single-week mover. global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 0.97->0.98 as the acute oil-shock drag unwinds (the Dow posted its best post-midterm day in 44 years, +3%/+1,569 on Nov 4 on gridlock optimism) - a small uptick, held to +0.01 by the Nov 5 risk-off reversal that wiped ~$2.5T from the Nasdaq on fears a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout, plus genuine divided-government and war-outcome uncertainty. Russia-Ukraine ground on at winter-campaign intensity - mass Russian strikes on the energy grid left 600,000+ without power in Dnipropetrovsk (DTEK), ~250,000 in Kharkiv, and blacked out central Kyiv (Nov 7), while Ukraine's deep-strike campaign hit the Kirishi/KINEF refinery in Leningrad Oblast (Nov 9) and ground combat stayed heaviest in the Pokrovsk/Kostiantynivka sectors (140 engagements Nov 8) - lifting cumulative conflict_deaths 1,561,000->1,564,000, a slightly sub-tempo +3,000 reflecting the Gulf front's cooling even as Ukraine stayed hot. Held steady: russia_stability stays 0.20 - the resuming refinery deep-strike campaign sustains economic pressure but is a continuation rather than a fresh discrete internal shock, and Russia's battlefield pressure at Pokrovsk offsets; food_security_index holds at 0.71 absent a fresh grain/supply signal. No new node: the midterms are a scheduled election (scored via governance/trust/growth, not a discrete era-defining node, consistent with this log's node discipline), and the Iran de-escalation remains an unconsummated turn - no signed US-Iran ceasefire, no reopening formalized, and no actual strike on nuclear sites (a consummated ceasefire or a major nuclear-site strike next week would each warrant one). Watched but not scored: the Nov 5 AI-buildout selloff is a markets signal scored via the growth modifier, not a frontier leap, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual damage surge; and regional seismicity (M6.1 near Fiji Nov 5, M5.7 central Japan Nov 8 injuring ~22, Vanuatu M6.2, continuing Flores aftershocks) was locally acute but, like prior quakes and cyclones in this stream, maps to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-11-09 to 11-16. A frozen-standoff, consolidation week: both wars ground on without a signed deal, and markets staged their first winning week since October. On the 2026 Iran war / Strait of Hormuz crisis, the de-escalation turn stalled into a 'no war, no peace' deadlock rather than consummating: Qatar's PM met Trump and Vance on Nov 9 and called the talks 'positive,' but Iran kept its seven conditions (end the naval blockade, lift sanctions, unfreeze funds, halt fighting on all fronts) while Secretary Rubio called the demands 'unacceptable' and Trump said 'no deal necessary' (sidelining the more dovish Vance). Crucially, kinetic fighting stayed low (only minor US actions - a blockade-running cargo vessel struck Nov 7) with no strike on Iranian nuclear sites, so nuclear_risk_level holds at 0.37 and middle_east_stability holds at 0.11 (the continued pause in major fighting is offset by the diplomatic hardening and persisting ship attacks - no decisive single-week mover). supply_chain_resilience holds at 0.41: markets are 'betting on peace' and Brent eased further to ~$96 (-~2.5% on the week), but the physical chokepoint stress did not actually resolve - the Washington Institute reported little sign of attacks abating in November after 37 ships were hit in October (the war's highest monthly total), three more tankers were damaged ~Nov 5, the US naval blockade held, JMIC kept its threat rating SEVERE, and ~490 vessels were waiting outside the strait with flows still well below prewar - so last week's jump to 0.41 (on the oil crash and recovering flows) already captured the relief and no further improvement is warranted while attacks persist. On Russia-Ukraine, the US-brokered Abu Dhabi talks (Nov 10-11) revived negotiations but produced only an in-principle large-scale prisoner swap and 'good momentum' rhetoric - no breakthrough on territory or security guarantees, with Russia still demanding Ukraine cede Donbas and drop NATO aspirations and ruling out meetings with Europeans - so it is an unconsummated development, not a ceasefire. Against that weak diplomacy, fresh signals of Russian internal strain accumulated: Ukrainian military intelligence reported Russia suffered its highest monthly casualties of the war in October, Ukraine's deep-strike campaign continued degrading the refining sector (an eighth 2026 strike on the Saratov refinery) atop a sector Kyiv already claims is ~51% offline, a prominent milblogger told Russians to prepare for hardship on Nov 9, and the Central Bank acknowledged the war's mounting economic effects - so russia_stability eases 0.20->0.19 (a small tick, with the Abu Dhabi momentum a partial offset). global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 0.98->0.99 as the oil-shock drag keeps unwinding: Wall Street posted its first winning week since October and biggest weekly gain since August (S&P 500 ~+2.5% to 7,561.67, Nasdaq's first weekly gain in five weeks) on falling oil and rotation out of megacap tech into staples/energy/communication services, even as a sharp Nvidia-led AI-valuation selloff (Nvidia -13% on the week, ~$820B wiped from AI names intra-week on leadership turmoil and debt-fuelled-buildout fears) and a hotter-than-expected October CPI (+0.4% m/m, core +0.3%, decelerating from September's +0.6% but above forecasts, Fed still hawkish into its Dec 8-9 meeting) kept the tick to +0.01. Sustained conflict (the hot Russia-Ukraine winter front - Russia's renewed grid campaign, heavy Pokrovsk/Kostiantynivka fighting - plus the lower-tempo but ongoing Hormuz maritime attacks) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,564,000->1,567,000, a sub-tempo +3,000 reflecting the Gulf front's continued cooling. No new node: no signed US-Iran or Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, no reopening of Hormuz formalized, no strike on Iranian nuclear sites, and no direct NATO-Russia war materialized - every thread remains a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis and 2022_russia_ukraine nodes, consistent with this log's node discipline (a consummated ceasefire or a major nuclear-site strike would each warrant one). Watched but not scored: governance_model (0.49) and us_institutional_trust (0.26) hold - the post-midterm Trump-Vance rift over Iran is political fallout already captured by last week's midterm moves, not a fresh discrete institutional event; the week's AI story was a markets/commercial one (Nvidia turmoil, Anthropic's upcoming IPO) with no frontier-capability flagship released in-window, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual damage surge; a wave of 50+ hoax bomb threats against European aircraft/airports (~Nov 6) was disruptive but maps to no clean structural dimension at meaningful magnitude; and no major earthquake or climate catastrophe landed in-window (early-November seismicity was routine; H5N1 poultry spread continued), so no climate/food/disaster mover - food_security_index holds at 0.71 absent a fresh grain signal.

Week of 2026-11-16 to 11-23. Two threads dominated: the sharpest Russia-Ukraine peace push of the war and a severe AI-driven market correction. The US tabled a 28-point peace plan (drafted Witkoff/Dmitriev) heavily favoring Russian demands - Ukraine to cede Donbas, cap its army, constitutionally renounce NATO, with Russian territorial recognition and sanctions relief / reintegration into the global economy - presented to Zelenskyy under a near-term deadline and then 'refined' in Geneva-style US-Ukraine talks, while the E3 (UK/France/Germany) scrambled a counter-framework and Zelenskyy pushed for a four-party (Ukraine-Europe-US-Russia) meeting 'as soon as possible.' Because the plan pressures a US ally into Russia-favorable terms while largely sidelining European allies (who publicly judged the draft unacceptable as written), it is a modest hit to Washington's alliance leadership: us_global_standing 0.55->0.54 (kept to -0.01 because the framework was being actively refined with Ukrainian input and Trump can still claim a peacemaker mantle, so it is strain rather than rupture). The credible, if contested, path to ending the largest active war - combined with continued Iran-front relief and no new NATO-Russia airspace incident - is the strongest multi-front de-escalation signal of the autumn, easing nuclear_risk_level 0.37->0.36 (held to -0.01 because fighting ran at winter-campaign intensity: Russia hit Ukraine's energy/gas network ~100 times in a week, Russian strikes killed 15+ in the Kyiv region on Nov 23, and no ceasefire was signed). On the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, diplomacy hardened (Trump said 'we don't need a deal,' Iran held to its seven conditions and said the strait would 'never return' to pre-war status, and Iran claimed two tankers hit mines on Nov 19) but kinetic tempo stayed low and the physical chokepoint measurably recovered - Hormuz throughput rebounded toward ~10M b/d with transits improving from October's ~4-vessels/day extreme (still ~65% below pre-conflict) and Brent crashed further to ~$88-92 (down ~19% on the month on recovering Gulf exports and a projected supply surplus) - so supply_chain_resilience ticks up 0.41->0.42, the first physical-flow improvement since the oil-price relief began (kept to +0.01 because the blockade still holds and attacks persist). Sustained two-front combat (the hot Russia-Ukraine winter grid campaign, Ukraine's deep-strike campaign now reaching Russian vessels in a Libyan port, and lower-tempo Hormuz maritime attacks) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,567,000->1,570,000, a sub-tempo +3,000 reflecting the Gulf front's continued cooling. Held steady: global_gdp_growth_modifier stays 0.99 - the week's defining macro event was a severe AI-valuation correction (S&P 500 into a >10% correction off its Oct 6 high, Nasdaq ~-18% from peak, Nvidia -47.5% from peak and -14% in its worst session in nearly two years amid a CEO scandal/resignation, ~$2.5T wiped from AI names) which is a real tightening of financial conditions and a negative wealth/sentiment shock, but it was squarely offset by the deepening oil-price relief (the single biggest real-economy drag of September-October unwinding hard) and a Monday Nov 23 rebound (S&P futures +2.6%), netting no decisive single-week growth mover; middle_east_stability holds at 0.11 (diplomatic hardening offset by oil relief, flow recovery and low kinetic tempo); russia_stability holds at 0.19 (the Russia-favorable peace framework is a diplomatic lifeline for Moscow but is unsigned and contested, roughly offsetting continued economic degradation - Ukraine's refinery deep-strike campaign and reported record monthly casualties - with no fresh discrete internal shock); governance_model (0.49) and us_institutional_trust (0.26) hold with no fresh institutional event. No new node: the 28-point plan is an unconsummated framework, not a signed ceasefire (a consummated Russia-Ukraine ceasefire next week would warrant a node), and the Hormuz fighting remains a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, consistent with this log's node discipline. Watched but not scored: the AI market correction is a markets/valuation event scored via the growth modifier - if it hardens into a confirmed systemic financial crisis (the 'AI bubble bursting') it would warrant an economic node, but as of this week it is a sharp correction with a Monday bounce, not a consummated crisis; the frontier-AI release cadence stayed incremental (OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol, Google Gemini 4 Neon, Alibaba Qwen 2.4T) after the early-September flagship wave already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick and global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0 absent an actual damage surge; and US Thanksgiving-week flooding (southern Florida evacuations Nov 18, deadly Southwest US flooding ~Nov 21) and El Nino-linked rains were regionally acute but, like prior regional weather in this stream, map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week - food_security_index holds at 0.71 absent a fresh grain signal.
